claims.title: Minimum-rate anchoring and decreasing-density NFA rounding propose polynomial-bit deadline log-probabilities

status: source_derived_unreviewed; Unreviewed source-reported proof candidate. Intake checks original bytes, derived page routes and repository integrity only. No independent proof reconstruction, external-theorem audit, diagnostic replay, validated implementation, practical acceleration or physical validation; correctness and historical priority UNKNOWN.
interface: For an explicitly represented finite source-target DAG with independent exponential activity durations, strictly positive rational rates and a rational deadline T supplied exactly in binary, the manuscript proposes a randomized polynomial-bit algorithm for U=Pr(longest source-target duration >=T). For rational epsilon>0 and 0<delta<1 it would output a binary rational ell with Pr[|ell-ln U|<=epsilon]>=1-delta when U>0, in time/bit work polynomial in graph size, total input bits, 1/epsilon and log(1/delta). It outputs -infinity for U=0 and ell=0 for T<=0 when a path exists. Missing path means U=0 by convention; for T>0 zero-only paths do not contribute. It computes log U without materializing a potentially enormous probability denominator. This is a proof candidate, not validated software or an established algorithmic advance.
limits: Independently reconstruct the anchored union/integration identity, simultaneous decreasing-density scaling, two-resource rounding and accepted-word NFA reduction. Audit conditional jitter, anti-concentration, confidence allocation and robust union estimation in the finite-bit model, including equal rates, zero connectors and extreme binary scales. Verify the exact #NFA theorem interface, recover the reported check code/raw receipts, and implement matched end-to-end benchmarks; review priority separately.
